subject: Sequenced MAP: pricing anchors, ramp milestones, and recommit pathway
messages:
From: Margaret Liu <mliu@horizonanalytics.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP and pricing anchors for pilot -> renewal uplift question

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers and the cost tooling look promising. We want to put a short mutual action plan (MAP) in place that ties our pilot acceptance criteria to clear commercial milestones. Two quick asks from our side:

1) Can you propose a pricing/commit ladder that maps to pilot->production ramp (pilot, initial commit, +50% ramp, full rollout)? We want to understand the discount tiers and any minimums.

2) We need visibility on how you treat renewal pricing: if we hit aggressive adoption (e.g., >2M tokens/month after 6 months), what controls are there on renewal uplift? We need a cap or a predictable formula for budgeting.

Also, procurement will need the MAP, a short SOW, and SOC2 summary to start an internal security review. Can you attach a one-page MAP and the SOC2 response?

Goal: sign pilot SOW the week of Sept 27 and run a 30-day pilot in Oct.

Thanks — Margaret

Margaret Liu
VP Product, Horizon Analytics
Margaret.Liu@horizonanalytics.com
+1 415-555-0198

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Margaret Liu <mliu@horizonanalytics.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP and pricing anchors for pilot -> renewal uplift question

Margaret — thanks, great to align. High level response below and I've attached a one-page MAP and SOC2 summary for procurement. See attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx, SOC2_response_summary.pdf.

Quick proposal (high level):
- Pilot (30 days): no upfront commit; reduced pilot rate (list * 0.75) with a pilot credit of $8k to offset token consumption during acceptance testing. Acceptance = 3 test prompts + latency SLA (p50 < 150ms) documented in MAP.
- Initial commit (Month 1 of GA): 100k tokens/day equivalent commit — priced at list * 0.85 (10% discount off list for volume + 5% onboarding credit applied to first invoice).
- Ramp milestone (reach 250k tokens/day sustained for 30 days): automatic discount step to list * 0.78; also qualify for dedicated support SLA and reduced overage rate.
- Full rollout (>=1.5M tokens/month sustained): custom enterprise pricing (case-by-case) with capped renewal uplift formula (see below).

Renewal uplift proposal (to address budget predictability):
- If usage increases by >30% year-over-year, renewal pricing may adjust up but capped at +15% YoY for the first two renewals.
- If we jointly agree to additional feature-based add-ons (private connectors, extended retention), those are itemized separately and excluded from the cap.

We can bake the pilot->commit ladder and the renewal cap into the SOW so procurement has certainty. Attaching SOW template with commercial placeholders; Ben will follow up with suggested language for the discount ladder and DocuSign link.

Next steps:
1) Review attached MAP_v1.xlsx and SOC2 summary (I included acceptance checklist and SLA metrics).
2) Ben will propose the SOW redlines and the DocuSign flow by EOD tomorrow.
3) If acceptable, aim to execute pilot SOW week of Sept 27.

Grace O'Connor
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

[attachment: SOC2_response_summary.pdf (pdf, 160KB)]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Margaret Liu <mliu@horizonanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP and pricing anchors for pilot -> renewal uplift question

Looping in a couple of clarifications on the discount ladder and risk controls — Margaret, copying here so procurement sees the logic.

- Discount ladder is volume-based and milestone-triggered. We always anchor on list when we communicate externally, but the effective price includes onboarding credits and pilot offset.
- Overage handling: during pilot we bill actual usage minus pilot credit. After commit, overages billed at the reduced overage rate for customers on a confirmed ramp path (we don't charge list overage if customer is actively enrolled in a MAP and hits ramp metrics).
- Renewal uplift cap (Grace's note is accurate): capped at +15% YoY for first two renewals if growth is organic and driven by the covered workloads. We reserve right to renegotiate if there are major new use-cases beyond the scope of the MAP.

Operational asks for procurement/security to close fast:
1) Confirm the list of test prompts they will use for acceptance (we included sample prompts in MAP_v1.xlsx).
2) Confirm region and data residency (we will run pilot in us-west-2 — does Horizon require EU hosting?).

I'll propose a short paragraph to insert in the SOW about renewal cap formula — Ben, can you draft and attach to the SOW before sending to DocuSign?

Sergio Alvarez
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP and pricing anchors for pilot -> renewal uplift question

Margaret — attaching a redlined SOW and a short commercial appendix (SOW_Redline_0926.docx). Highlights:
- Commercial appendix includes the exact discount ladder wording, ramp triggers, and the renewal uplift cap language (capped at +15% YoY for two renewals; renewal increases for feature add-ons excluded).
- Added a simple formula example so FP&A at Horizon can model: 
  Effective renewal price = prior term price * (1 + min(0.15, measured_usage_growth)) + addons
- Included a clause that guarantees a 30-day notice before any material pricing changes at renewal plus an escalations contact.

Ben will start the DocuSign package as soon as we get a 'go' from your procurement team. DocuSign link will include SOW + commercial appendix + MAP_v1.xlsx.

From: Margaret Liu <mliu@horizonanalytics.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 20:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP and pricing anchors for pilot -> renewal uplift question

Thanks Grace, Sergio, Ben — the MAP and redlined SOW look reasonable. Procurement has two small asks before we sign:

1) Can you add an explicit definition of "covered workloads" in the MAP so the renewal cap can't be applied to unrelated new use-cases (we suggested language in the attached comment).
2) Can Horizon get a one-time exception on the renewal cap if an acquisition drives >200% usage growth in a single year? We propose a mutual notification + 60-day renegotiation window.

If you accept those two changes, we can sign the pilot SOW by Sept 24. Pilot schedule still Oct 4 start.

Margaret

Margaret Liu
VP Product, Horizon Analytics
